reason: This passage from Ezra 3 describes the return from exile and rebuilding of the Temple under the leadership of Joshua son of Jozadak and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel. The leadership model presented focuses on religious devotion, organizational cooperation, and unity of the people gathering as one (כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד) to rebuild the altar and restore worship. While the text mentions fear (אֵימָה) that the people felt regarding surrounding nations, it contains no description of violence employed by leaders, nor any model of leadership through violence toward unruly or disobedient people. The passage emphasizes construction, religious observance, and celebration rather than punishment or coercion.
